chief_complaint: incidental 3.5 cm right upper lobe spiculated lung mass found on CT scan requiring surgical staging and lobectomy
hpi_details: 64F with 45 pack-year smoking history underwent CT chest for screening which revealed an incidental 3.5 cm spiculated, solid mass in the anterior segment of the right upper lobe. PET-CT confirms avid hypermetabolic uptake in the RUL mass (SUV max 11.4) without mediastinal lymph node uptake or distant metastases. Bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy confirms Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (Lung Adenocarcinoma).
ideas: terrified of having lung cancer and dying from metastatic disease
concerns: worried about losing a lobe of her lung and whether she will be able to breathe normally after surgery
expectations: wants complete surgical removal of the cancer as quickly as possible with robotic or minimally invasive technique
social_hx: Retired accountant, former smoker (quit 2 months ago)

available_results.value: 3.5 cm right-upper-lobe mass with SUVmax 11.4; no avid mediastinal nodes or distant metastases
FEV1 2.1 L (78% predicted); DLCO 72% predicted; predicted postoperative FEV1 and DLCO both >60%

clinical_knowledge.topic: Resectable Stage IB Lung Adenocarcinoma evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Resectable Stage IB Lung Adenocarcinoma is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Schedule for Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery (VATS) or Robotic-Assisted Right Upper Lobectomy with systematic mediastinal lymph node dissection (stations 2R, 4R, 7, 10R, 11R), adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: incidental 3.5 cm right upper lobe spiculated lung mass found on CT scan requiring surgical staging and lobectomy

Key HPI features: 64F with 45 pack-year smoking history underwent CT chest for screening which revealed an incidental 3.5 cm spiculated, solid mass in the anterior segment of the right upper lobe. PET-CT confirms avid hypermetabolic uptake in the RUL mass (SUV max 11.4) without mediastinal lymph node uptake or distant metastases. Bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy confirms Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (Lung Adenocarcinoma).

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: HR 76, BP 130/82, SpO2 96% on room air. Pulmonary function tests (PFTs): FEV1 2.1 L (78% predicted), DLCO 72% predicted. Quantitative perfusion lung scan confirms predicted postoperative (ppo) FEV1 > 60% and ppo DLCO > 60%, confirming excellent physiologic reserve for anatomical lobectomy. Endobronchial Ultrasound (EBUS) mediastinal staging negative for N2/N3 lymph node involvement.
Current medications: Tiotropium inhaler daily, Lisinopril 10mg daily
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Resectable Stage IB Lung Adenocarcinoma.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Benign granuloma (ruled out by biopsy) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: New bone pain or neurological symptoms — would suggest metastatic spread requiring re-staging.
management_principles: Schedule for Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery (VATS) or Robotic-Assisted Right Upper Lobectomy with systematic mediastinal lymph node dissection (stations 2R, 4R, 7, 10R, 11R)
Provide preoperative pulmonary rehabilitation and incentive spirometry counseling
Assess clinical stability, monitor vital parameters, and perform targeted diagnostic investigations.
Implement targeted therapeutic interventions per evidence-based clinical practice guidelines.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 64F presenting with biopsy-proven Clinical Stage IB (cT2a N0 M0) Right Upper Lobe Lung Adenocarcinoma undergoing surgical resectability and cardiopulmonary tolerance assessment.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: HR 76, BP 130/82, SpO2 96% on room air. Pulmonary function tests (PFTs): FEV1 2.1 L (78% predicted), DLCO 72% predicted. Quantitative perfusion lung scan confirms predicted postoperative (ppo) FEV1 > 60% and ppo DLCO > 60%, confirming excellent physiologic reserve for anatomical lobectomy. Endobronchial Ultrasound (EBUS) mediastinal staging negative for N2/N3 lymph node involvement.
reference_soap.assessment: Resectable Clinical Stage IB Lung Adenocarcinoma of the Right Upper Lobe with good cardiopulmonary reserve.
reference_soap.plan: Schedule for Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery (VATS) or Robotic-Assisted Right Upper Lobectomy with systematic mediastinal lymph node dissection (stations 2R, 4R, 7, 10R, 11R). Provide preoperative pulmonary rehabilitation and incentive spirometry counseling.

learning_objectives: Interpret preoperative cardiopulmonary risk stratification parameters for major lung resection (FEV1 and DLCO thresholds >60% predicted vs requirement for exercise testing VO2 max)
Explain the oncological superiority of anatomical lobectomy plus mediastinal lymphadenectomy over wedge/sublobar resection for T1/T2 non-small cell lung cancer
Understand the role of invasive mediastinal staging (EBUS-TBNA or mediastinoscopy) prior to surgical resection
Compare minimally invasive (VATS/Robotic) vs open thoracotomy techniques regarding pain, hospital stay, and recovery

teaching.one_liner: A confirmed non-small cell lung cancer without lymph node or distant spread, best treated with surgical lobectomy and lymph node dissection while cure is still possible.
red_flags: New bone pain or neurological symptoms — would suggest metastatic spread requiring re-staging

must_ask.say: How many years and how much have you smoked?
Did you have any symptoms, or was this found on a screening scan?
Any cough, coughing up blood, or breathlessness?
What worries you most about losing part of your lung?
How is your breathing with everyday activities now?
